## Proposition: local exact quotient for suffix feasibility

For a fixed original germ subset S and remaining depth d, the inherited R247/R303 predicate C_d first rejects when c(S)>2^d-1, accepts optimistically when c(S)<=d, and otherwise tries the appropriate frozen library (saturated wall library if c(S)=2^d-1; full linear library otherwise). For a split (L+,L-), let q_S(L) be the unordered pair {S intersect L+, S intersect L-}, preserving both complete germ masks (including empty masks). Two splits with equal q_S have the same child label capacities and the same two recursive truth values, since the recursive predicate depends only on the child germ set and depth, not the preceding split identity. Thus the existential over splits factors exactly through q_S, with no change to C_d. Both zero-germ exclusions and original support provenance are retained; zero set within S is reconstructed as S minus the union of the two children. This is a local observer quotient, not a global identification of observation directions, not valid if a later predicate additionally depends on the path of split identities. An injective encoding is min(x,y) OR (max(x,y) << 98) for 98-bit masks. Saturation library selection is unchanged. On cutoff, unfinished states are unknown and never cached false.

This optimization avoids repeated capacity or recursive checks for identical restricted splits but still visits every raw library entry as necessary, constructs a set for each nontrivial state, and incurs BigInt encoding/hash costs. No wall-time speedup is asserted. Exact outcome equivalence tested on the same first 64 direct residual candidates with both modes, including their propagated deltas and failure cores. Full run raw split budget 5,000,000. Historical exclusion validity remains inherited, not independently reviewed.
